exercises.name: Standing Leg Curls

source_english.description: A standing leg curl on a machine bends one knee against a padded lever while the thigh stays vertical.
instructions: Adjust the machine pad behind one ankle and hold the support handles upright.
Keep the working thigh against the pad and bend the knee to draw the heel toward the glute.
Pause at the top without moving the hip.
Lower the lever slowly, complete the side, and switch legs.
form_cues: Point the knee toward the floor.
common_mistakes: Extending the hip to swing the lever.
source_english.safety_note: Use a load that lets the knee move smoothly without the pelvis rotating.

source_english.description: The Air Bike combines seated pedaling with reciprocal push-pull handle strokes, so the legs and arms share the conditioning effort.
instructions: Adjust the machine so the seat allows a slight bend in the knee at the bottom of each pedal stroke.
Sit upright, place your feet on the pedals, and grip the moving handles.
Pedal while pushing and pulling the handles in a smooth reciprocal rhythm.
Maintain the planned pace for the duration, then ease off gradually.
common_mistakes: Relying only on the arms or only on the legs.
Stopping abruptly after a hard interval.
source_english.safety_note: Adjust the seat before starting and keep the handles moving smoothly during hard intervals.

dataset_instruction_steps_read: Set up a bar at waist height or use a suspension trainer.
Stand facing the bar or suspension trainer, with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grab the bar or handles with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Lean back, keeping your body straight and your heels on the ground.
Pull your chest towards the bar or handles, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower yourself back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
